title: Lion Nebula (NIRCam + MIRI image)
credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI. Image Processing: A. Pagan (STScI)

geometryEvidence.reference: A picture of the sky: the plane is the picture's own tangent plane, perpendicular to the sight line through the picture's centre, so it faces the Sun. That centre is 1.2 arcsec from the star, which is the whole of the recipe's inclination. Not the orientation of the object itself.

registration.method: The file's embedded sky tags for scale and direction, 0.0304 arcsec per pixel and north 170.0° left of vertical, and the star for place: the star in the picture, the largest patch of saturated pixels within 1 arcsec of where the tags put it, 51 px, pixel 1733.9, 1715.5, is set at the recipe's target, so the frame's centre is 112.2950734°, 20.9120789°. The tags alone put the star 0.22 arcsec from where the picture shows it.

displayModel: Inside the outer shell's outline, a circle of 23 arcsec, the picture's light lies on two walls, in front of the star and behind it: the outer shell's, a sphere, and inside the inner shell's outline that shell's, a prolate spheroid pointed almost at the Sun. Measured radial velocities say which of the inner shell's walls a feature is on. The fine detail between the two shells lies on one surface: the shells' equatorial plane where the measured structures are at rest, bent toward the outer shell's near wall or its far wall where they approach or recede. Outside the outer shell the picture lies on one plane facing the Sun.
coverage: The published frame inside a circle about the star: the picture fades out between 46.8 and 52 arcsec from the star, the largest circle the frame holds, so no straight edge shows.

acquisition.operation: Download the publisher's JPEG; no crop or resample.
